title: Choosing a Guardian Worksheet
description: Questions to help parents compare possible guardians for minor children and pick a first choice and a backup.
intro: Choosing who would raise your children is often the hardest decision in a plan. This worksheet helps you compare candidates side by side. Fill it out for each person you are considering, then talk with your top choice before naming them.

sections.heading: Values and parenting
items: Does this person share your core values and beliefs?
How do they approach discipline, education, and screen time?
How would they keep your children connected to your memory and extended family?
Would they respect your religious or cultural wishes for the children?
How do your children feel about this person?

sections.heading: Practical situation
items: Where do they live, and would your children have to move schools?
Do they have room in their home for your children?
How old are they, and how is their health?
Do they already have children, and how would the families blend?
How demanding is their work schedule?

sections.heading: Relationships
items: If the candidate is a couple, would you still want either one if they separated?
Could they work well with the person managing the children's money?
Would they keep your children in touch with grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins?
Is there any family conflict that could lead to a challenge?

sections.heading: Money and support
items: Could they raise your children without financial strain if funds were provided?
Would they be comfortable having a separate trustee manage the money?
What expenses would you want covered, such as a bigger home or car?
Have you estimated what it would cost using the guardian fund calculator?

sections.heading: Next steps
items: Rank your first choice and a backup
Ask your first choice if they are willing to serve
Write a short letter to the guardian about your hopes for your children
Name the guardian and backup in your will
Revisit your choice every few years or when circumstances change
